Demolition types

Find the demolition that matches your structure

Six pages, each one about a different kind of structure. If you are not sure which one you are looking at, call and describe it.

Residential

Residential Demolition Houses, duplex sites and knockdown rebuilds Single and double storey, brick, fibro and timber frame. Partial Demolition Extensions, garages, sheds and pools Where part of the structure stays and has to be protected.

Commercial and industrial

Commercial and Industrial Demolition Shops, warehouses and factories Structural steel, concrete frames and plant, staged around access. Service Station Demolition Service stations and fuel sites Including underground fuel tank removal and the validation that follows.

Specialist

Multi-Unit and Apartment Block Demolition Walk ups and unit blocks Redevelopment sites where the block comes down in a planned sequence. Hand Demolition Tight access and precision work Taken apart by hand where a machine cannot reach or cannot be trusted.

Scoping

What actually changes the price and the programme

Two houses on the same street can be a week apart in programme and a long way apart in cost. The structure itself is rarely the reason. These are:

  • Access. What size machine can get in, and whether material has to be carried out rather than loaded where it falls. A zero tail swing machine changes what is possible on a narrow block.
  • What it is built from. Double brick, timber frame, concrete, structural steel and fibro all come down differently and go to different places.
  • Hazardous material. Anything built before the late 1980s is assumed to contain asbestos until it is tested. The testing happens before demolition, not during it.
  • What stays. A shared wall, a retained extension, a fence, a tree, a pool or a neighbouring building all turn a knockdown into selective work.
  • Services. Power, water, gas and sewer have to be disconnected by the relevant authority before anything starts.
  • Where the spoil goes. Clean fill, mixed demolition waste and contaminated material have different destinations and very different costs.

We would rather walk the site and tell you which of these apply than send a number that changes later.

Who holds what on an asbestos job

Identification and sampling
Accredited testing laboratory
Removal of bonded and friable material
Licensed asbestos removalist
Air monitoring and clearance certificate
Independent licensed assessor
Transport and disposal
Licensed waste facility
Demolition once clearance is issued
Max Demolition and Excavation, demolition licence AD214737

We coordinate every step above and hold the demolition licence only. The asbestos licence, the monitoring and the clearance sit with the specialists named against them.

Before the machine arrives

Asbestos comes out first, and it is not us who hold that licence

Most Sydney housing stock built before 1990 has asbestos somewhere in it. Eaves, fibro sheeting, wet area linings, vinyl floor tiles, roof sheets, fencing. It has to be identified and removed before demolition proper, and it cannot go in with general waste.

We manage that whole pathway as part of the contract: identification, sampling, removal by licensed asbestos removalists, independent air monitoring and clearance, and disposal at a licensed facility. The removal work itself is carried out by licensed specialists and the clearance certificate is issued independently.

Why this matters to your programme

Asbestos found after demolition has started stops the job. Testing before we mobilise costs very little and is the single most common reason a demolition runs late.

Asbestos Services

How it runs

From the first site visit to a block you can build on

The same five steps on a garage and on a factory. Only the duration and the paperwork change.

01

Site visit and scope

We walk the site, look at access, what is standing, what stays and what is underneath, and scope the demolition, the hazardous material and the cartage together.

02

Approvals, services and notifications

Demolition approval, service disconnections with each authority, and the SafeWork notification where the work requires it. These set the start date.

03

Hazardous material removal

Asbestos removed by licensed removalists under the control measures the material requires, then independent air monitoring and a clearance certificate before anything else happens.

04

Demolition and load out

The structure comes down in a controlled order with material separated as it falls, so concrete, steel and timber leave the site on different trucks to different destinations.

05

Clear, level and hand back

Site cleared, ground left graded and at the level your engineer specified, and the disposal dockets handed over with it.

Waste and recycling

Where demolition waste actually goes

Sorting on site costs machine time and saves tipping fees. On most jobs it is the cheaper of the two.

MaterialWhere it comes fromPathway
Clean concrete and brickSlabs, footings, walls, driveways Crushed and recycled as road base or aggregate
Structural steel and metalsFraming, roof sheeting, fixtures, reinforcement Separated on site and sold into scrap recovery
Clean timberFraming, flooring, joinery Recovered where it is sound, mulched or landfilled where it is not
Mixed demolition wastePlaster, insulation, carpet, fit out Sorted at a licensed waste facility
Asbestos and bonded fibroEaves, sheeting, roofing, wet areas, fencing Wrapped, labelled, transported and buried at a licensed facility only
Contaminated soilFuel sites, fill of unknown origin, old industrial ground Classified, then disposed of at a facility licensed for that classification

The cartage is on the same contract

Truck and dog, bogie and 10 wheeler tippers, so the spoil leaves as it is generated rather than sitting on the block waiting for a separate contractor.

Who we work for

Three different briefs, one contractor

Builders and Developers Programme driven work where the demolition, the dig and the cartage have to line up. Homeowners Knockdown rebuilds, garages, sheds and pools on a property somebody lives in. About and our equipment The licence, the corridor we cover and the machines that do the work.

What usually comes next

Before you book

What people ask before they book a demolition

How long does a house demolition take on site?
The machine work on an ordinary single storey house is usually one to three days. What sets the overall programme is everything before it: service disconnections booked with the authority, asbestos identified and removed under clearance, and the approval in hand. Those run in weeks, not days, and they are outside anyone's control once they are lodged.
Do I need the services disconnected before you start?
Yes. Power, water, gas and sewer all have to be disconnected or made safe by the relevant authority before demolition begins. Start them as soon as you have approval, because the lead time belongs to the authority and not to the demolisher.
What happens if asbestos is found after the job starts?
Work stops. That is the single most common reason a demolition runs late, and it is why testing happens before we mobilise rather than during. A hazardous materials survey on a pre 1990 property costs very little against the cost of a stopped site.
Can you demolish one part of a building and leave the rest?
Yes. Partial and hand demolition both exist for that. The section being kept is braced and protected first, and the work next to it is done in an order that does not load it.
Do you take the slab and the footings as well?
That is a scope decision rather than a technical one. Removing the slab, the footings and the driveway costs more in both machine time and cartage, so it is priced as a separate line and you decide. Tell us what your builder needs and we will quote it that way.
Who is responsible for the fencing and the hoarding?
We are, for the duration of our works, unless your contract says otherwise. Site fencing, dust and sediment control and protection of the adjoining property are scoped with the demolition and not left to be sorted out on the day.
